doc.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024

title: Kenton's lugubrious swing
summary: Slow versus fast, and Kenton's brass-heavy band as dragging a water buffalo; Stan was a great leader.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: So is it harder to play slow music than fast music, or vice versa?

Not really. I learned that too, when with Kenton’s band you had to push. Because Kenton’s band was like dragging a dead water buffalo through the mud. I mean it was so brass heavy you know. And I don’t say that in a disparaging way. It had its own way of swinging, it was just sort of lugubrious swing.
Lugubrious swing. There’s another quote from Ed Soph.
But now Stan was a great leader. And the band was a real challenge in many ways, which would be another six hours. But — now I’ve lost my train of thought when I was coming back to Woody’s band.
Well we were talking about swing and Stan.
